GPX track segment duration calculation returns negative values

#### Description

When calculating the duration of a GPX track segment, the `get_duration()` method returns negative values instead of positive durations.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
import gpxpy
import datetime

# Create a simple GPX track with two points
gpx = gpxpy.GPX()
gpx.tracks.append(gpxpy.GPXTrack())
gpx.tracks[0].segments.append(gpxpy.GPXTrackSegment())

# Add two points with a 1 minute time difference
gpx.tracks[0].segments[0].points.append(
    gpxpy.GPXTrackPoint(
        latitude=12, 
        longitude=13, 
        time=datetime.datetime(2013, 1, 1, 12, 30)
    )
)
gpx.tracks[0].segments[0].points.append(
    gpxpy.GPXTrackPoint(
        latitude=12, 
        longitude=13, 
        time=datetime.datetime(2013, 1, 1, 12, 31)
    )
)

# This should return 60 seconds but returns -60 instead
duration = gpx.get_duration()
print(f"Duration: {duration}")  # Expected: 60, Actual: -60
```

The duration calculation is returning negative values when it should return positive durations representing the time elapsed between the first and last points in the track.
</issue>
